subject: Post-demo: Latency & throughput benchmarks / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>, Kelly Rogers <kelly.rogers@globex.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Latency & throughput benchmarks / next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you a direct apples-to-apples comparison against the hyperscaler setup you mentioned.

Recap (call highlights)
- Scope: inference for customer-facing chat (max seq len 2048), internal background batching for indexing/embeddings.
- Goals: match p95/p99 latency SLOs for 99% of requests, and validate sustained tokens/sec for peak windows (burst to 10k tokens/sec).
- Competitors on your shortlist: AWS SageMaker/Endpoint (g5/inf1), Google Vertex AI.

Immediate ask from Globex
1) Side-by-side p95/p99 latency at seq len 512 and 2048 (single-stream and 8-concurrent streams).
2) Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at batch sizes 1, 8, 32 for your typical prompts.
3) Cost estimate (USD per 1M tokens) for each configuration.

Proposed next tests (what we suggest Redwood run)
- A/B: Redwood hosted API vs Globex’s current hyperscaler baseline (you shared recent traces)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory/KV cache hit rate
- Models: open model variant you requested (quantized v1) + unquantized baseline
- Timebox: 48 hours of sustained runs for throughput curves, plus synthetic tail-latency runs

Attached: redwood-globex-benchmarks-20260401.pdf (summary of our preliminary runs), redwood-compare-hyperscaler-summary.pdf

Next steps
- If that test matrix looks good, can we lock in a 48-hour window next Tue/Wed (4/7-4/8) for the run?
- Please confirm which AWS/Vertex instance types you want us to match for cost numbers (you mentioned g5.2xlarge / n1-standard-16 as examples).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi and Dev to own the run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0128
Redwood Inference

From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kelly Rogers <kelly.rogers@globex.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Latency & throughput benchmarks / next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions before we lock in the run window:

1) For the p95/p99 comparisons, can you also include the hyperscaler’s managed endpoint numbers with their autoscaling profile (we've seen long tails during scale-up)? Specifically we want to see the behavior during 5x sudden load increases.
2) For tokens/sec, our internal traffic is highly spiky: 80% of traffic is short (avg 120 tokens), 20% long (avg 1,200 tokens). Can you capture both distributions and include separate cost projections?
3) For cost, please show normalized USD / 1M tokens as you mentioned — include both compute and networking assumptions.
4) SLA question: if we find a regression post-rollout, what is your rollback cadence and how fast can you failover to a fallback model/region?

If those look reasonable, 4/7-4/8 works for us. We prefer runs during our daytime (09:00 - 18:00 ET) so we can watch dashboards.

Also, can you include any p95/p99 examples vs the managed AWS/Vertex endpoints? We want to see tail behavior, not just averages.

—Amit
Amit Shah
Director, Platform Engineering | Globex Corporation
amit.shah@globex.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@globex.com>, Kelly Rogers <kelly.rogers@globex.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Latency & throughput benchmarks / next steps

Appreciate the detail, Amit — good points. Below is an explicit test plan we’ll run and a short SLA/failover note.

Test plan (detailed)
- Tail-latency test: 5 cycles of 5x sudden load increases (ramp 1x -> 5x in 30s) to capture autoscale tail behavior. Measure p95/p99 and p99.9.
- Distribution tests: two traffic profiles (short-heavy and long-heavy) matching your percentages. Report tokens/sec and cost per profile.
- Concurrency matrix: single-stream, 8 concurrent streams, 32 concurrent streams.
- Batch sizes: 1, 8, 32.
- Models: open-model-quant-v1 (our recommended quantized profile), open-model-base (unquantized).
- Outputs: CSVs for latencies, tokens/sec time series, GPU utilization traces, KV cache hit rates, and cost calc sheet.

SLA & rollback behavior (summary)
- Rollback cadence: we can roll traffic back to the prior model variant within 1-2 minutes using our routing policies; full region failover within 10 minutes if needed (depends on customer routing acceptance).
- Canary policy: we’ll start with 10% traffic for any rollout and step to 100% with automated guardrails on latency/regression alerts.

Proposed schedule: run tests 2026-04-07 09:00 ET — 2026-04-08 17:00 ET (we’ll stream dashboards). Please confirm and we’ll create a shared dashboard and a Doc with runbook + links.

Links & attachments
- Preliminary benchmark summary (attached)
- Shared runbook and dashboards: https://redwood-internal.example.com/benchmarks/globex/20260401

If that’s green, Rishi & Dev will own execution — Rishi can you take the tail-latency runs and Dev can own cost calc & data collection?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
